title: Read the charts
summary: Learn what the fitness and species charts tell you, and what they cannot.

steps.title: When the best line goes flat
steps.body:
The fitness chart has a solid line for the best car of each generation, and lines for the median and the average car below it. A big gap means a few leaders are far ahead of the rest. When the median climbs toward the best, the whole population is catching up.

When the best line stays flat for many generations, evolution is stuck. `stagnation` counts those generations: it is 0 right after a new record.

Add an `if` that mutates harder once `stagnation` passes 10. Later calls in the block override earlier ones, so put it after the `breed` you already have.

check.message: Add an if inside each generation that reads stagnation.

hints: An if looks like if condition { ... }, and the breed call goes inside the braces.
Add if stagnation > 10 { breed(mutate: { weights: 0.9, addConnection: 0.08, addNode: 0.06 }) }.

steps.title: When the species bands thin out
steps.body:
The species chart stacks one colored band per species, in the color its cars wear on the track. Wide bands are big species. When the chart shrinks to one or two bands, nearly every brain is a variation of the same idea, and there is little left for evolution to try.

`species.count` is the number of bands. Add an `if` that aims for 12 species whenever there are fewer than 3.

check.message: Add an if inside each generation that reads species.count.

hints: This is the same shape as the stagnation rule, with speciate inside.

steps.title: Memorizing one road
steps.body:
Every chart you have seen measures the training road. A brain that trains on one road for long enough learns that road, quirks and all. Fitness keeps climbing, yet on a new road it can crash at the first bend it does not know. This is called overfitting.

Mix in a new random road every 10 generations. The chart will dip each time the road changes. That dip is the honest number: it shows how the brains drive somewhere new.

The Bench tab goes further and tests a brain on roads that training never uses.
hints: generation % 10 == 0 is true every 10th generation. Skip generation 0, the very first one.
Add if generation % 10 == 0 and generation > 0 { randomTrack(seed: generation) } after useTrack.
